newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen aiming for 2,700 points next week.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen aiming for 2,700 points next week.

text.p: The German DAX index of leading shares is expected to recover from losses posted on Wednesday and once-again tackle the crucial 2,700 point level next week, traders said on Friday.
Dealers said the fall of over one percent on Wednesday, promted by a dive in shares in SAP AG on a profits warning, had actually been healthy for the market.
"We've had a good shake out. After a couple of days range trading we should be ready to head upwards again," said one.
The IBIS DAX, which measures all-day electronic dealings in the DAX index, traded just 0.30 points off at 2,681.64.

The DAX started trade on Friday weighed down by weakness on Wall Street and Japan's Nikkei index, but recovered its losses after comments by Bundesbank council members suggested further interest rate cuts could not be ruled out.
The comments boosted Bunds, which had dropped on Wednesday after Buba economist Otmar Issing said rates were at an historic low and "nothing more is to be expected or necessary."

The DAX had reached a record level of 2,739.26 points in floor trade last week and dealers had expected a period of consolidation below the new highs, but said the longer-term outlook was still positive.
Deutsche Babcock AG was one of the day's main losers, down over eight percent, or 3.50 marks, to 39.50 in IBIS dealings amid insolvency speculation.
But the stock had recovered somewhat from an all-time low of 30 marks hit in early electronic trade after the firm said the rumours were completely unfounded.
